title: TCP Discipline — Tax Compliance and Planning

questions.q: For 2026, at what level of taxable income is the §199A deduction of a single filer operating a specified service trade or business fully phased out?
questions.why: 2026 threshold for single is $201,775 with a phase-in range widened by OBBBA to $75,000. Full phase-out at $201,775 + $75,000 = $276,775. Above that, an SSTB gets no deduction regardless of wages or UBIA.

questions.q: A non-SSTB business owner is above the §199A threshold. The deduction is limited to the greater of:

choices.A: 50% of W-2 wages, or 25% of W-2 wages plus 2.5% of UBIA of qualified property
choices.B: 20% of W-2 wages, or 10% of UBIA
choices.C: 50% of QBI, or 25% of taxable income
choices.D: There is no wage limitation for non-SSTBs

questions.why: The wage/UBIA limitation phases in above the threshold. This is why paying W-2 wages can increase the QBI deduction, and why setting an S corp salary too low can reduce it.

questions.q: New for 2026 under OBBBA, a taxpayer with at least $1,000 of active qualified business income receives:

choices.C: An exemption from the SSTB limitation

questions.why: The $400 minimum deduction applies from 2026 when active QBI is at least $1,000.

questions.q: Which business would NOT qualify as a qualified trade or business for §1202 purposes?

choices.A: A software company selling a SaaS product

questions.why: Consulting is expressly disqualified, along with health, law, engineering, architecture, accounting, actuarial science, performing arts, athletics, financial services, and brokerage, plus any business whose principal asset is the reputation or skill of its employees.

questions.q: A founder receives QSBS at original issuance after July 4, 2025 and sells at a gain four years later. Under OBBBA, the exclusion percentage is:

choices.A: 0%, because the five-year holding period was not met

questions.why: OBBBA created a tiered exclusion for stock acquired after 2025-07-04: 50% at three years, 75% at four, 100% at five. Stock acquired on or before that date keeps the all-or-nothing five-year rule. VERIFY against primary text before filing.

questions.q: A taxpayer sells QSBS held for 18 months and wants to avoid recognizing the gain. The correct mechanism and deadline are:

choices.B: §1045 rollover into new QSBS within 60 days
choices.D: No deferral is available before five years

questions.why: §1045 permits rollover of QSBS gain into other QSBS within 60 days if the original stock was held more than six months. The holding period tacks, preserving progress toward the exclusion.

questions.q: An employee receives restricted stock subject to vesting. The §83(b) election must be filed within:

choices.A: 30 days of the transfer, with no extensions available
choices.C: The due date of the return for the year of transfer
choices.D: 30 days of the first vesting date

questions.why: Thirty days from transfer, strictly enforced, no relief for a late election. Missing it means ordinary income at each vesting tranche at then-current FMV and delays the QSBS holding period. Form 15620 may be used; send certified mail and retain the receipt.

questions.q: For 2026, a 52-year-old self-employed individual with ample net earnings maintains a solo 401(k). What is the maximum total annual addition including the catch-up contribution?
questions.why: 2026 §415(c) total annual addition limit is $72,000, and the age-50 catch-up of $8,000 is on top of that limit. $72,000 + $8,000 = $80,000. The employee deferral component is $24,500 + $8,000.

questions.q: A taxpayer with a $200,000 pre-tax rollover IRA makes a $7,500 nondeductible traditional IRA contribution and immediately converts $7,500 to a Roth. The taxable portion of the conversion is approximately:

choices.C: About $7,229, because of the pro-rata rule

questions.why: All traditional IRAs are aggregated. Basis is $7,500 of $207,500 total, so only about 3.6% of the conversion is tax-free; roughly $7,229 is taxable. Rolling the pre-tax IRA into a 401(k) first removes it from the calculation.

questions.q: The best year to execute a large Roth conversion is generally one in which the taxpayer:

choices.B: Has an NOL or unusually low income
choices.C: Is about to sell a business at a large gain

questions.why: Conversions fill low brackets permanently. A loss year or pre-revenue year is the ideal window. Note that recharacterization of conversions was repealed, so the conversion is irrevocable once made.

questions.q: A profitable business owner is deciding between operating as a C corporation and as an S corporation. The C corporation is generally superior when:

choices.A: All earnings will be distributed to the owner annually
choices.B: Earnings are retained and reinvested in the business
choices.C: The owner wants to minimize payroll taxes
choices.D: The owner wants to deduct losses currently

questions.why: The 21% flat rate beats individual rates only when earnings stay inside. Distributed earnings suffer double tax approaching 40%. Retained earnings also raise §531 accumulated earnings exposure above the credit, and C corp losses are trapped at the entity level.

questions.q: An S corporation shows $300,000 of net profit and pays its sole owner-employee a $20,000 salary while distributing the rest. The principal exposure is:

choices.B: Recharacterization of distributions as wages, with payroll tax, interest and penalties

questions.cite: IRC §162(a)(1); Watson v. United States, 668 F.3d 1008 (8th Cir. 2012)
questions.why: Unreasonably low officer compensation is the leading S corp audit issue. A low wage also shrinks the §199A W-2 wage limitation, so it can cost more than it saves at higher income.

questions.q: Place the loss limitation gates in the order they are applied to a pass-through business loss.

choices.A: At-risk, basis, passive activity, excess business loss
choices.B: Basis, at-risk, passive activity, excess business loss
choices.C: Passive activity, basis, at-risk, excess business loss
choices.D: Excess business loss, basis, at-risk, passive activity

questions.why: Basis first, then at-risk, then passive activity, then the excess business loss cap. Amounts disallowed by §461(l) become an NOL carryforward under §172.

questions.q: A post-2020 federal net operating loss carryforward may offset what portion of taxable income?

choices.B: 80% of taxable income determined without regard to the NOL deduction

questions.why: 80% limitation, indefinite carryforward, no carryback for most taxpayers. This changes the value of accelerating deductions into a loss year.

questions.q: A pass-through entity tax (PTET) election benefits the owner because:

choices.A: It reduces the entity's federal taxable income by a state tax deduction not subject to the §164 SALT cap, with a state credit to the owner
choices.B: It exempts the owner from state tax entirely
choices.C: It converts ordinary income to capital gain

questions.why: The entity-level payment is a business deduction, bypassing the individual SALT cap, and the owner takes a state credit. Blessed by Notice 2020-75 and preserved by OBBBA. The New York election deadline is March 15 of the tax year and is irrevocable.

questions.q: For 2026, a single taxpayer with MAGI of $200,000 received $30,000 of qualified tips. Compute the allowable Schedule 1-A tips deduction.
questions.why: Maximum is $25,000, reduced $100 for each $1,000 of MAGI over $150,000. Excess = $50,000 = 50 increments x $100 = $5,000. $25,000 - $5,000 = $20,000. Married taxpayers must file jointly to claim it.

questions.q: A taxpayer wants to donate appreciated stock held three years to a public charity. The optimal treatment is:

choices.A: Sell the stock, recognize the gain, and donate the cash
choices.B: Donate the stock directly, deducting fair market value and avoiding the built-in gain, limited to 30% of AGI
choices.C: Donate the stock, deducting basis only
choices.D: Donate to a private foundation for a higher AGI limit

questions.why: Long-term capital gain property donated to a public charity is deducted at FMV with no recognition of the gain, subject to a 30%-of-AGI limit and a five-year carryforward. Depreciated property should be sold first so the loss is usable.

questions.q: A pre-revenue startup with no income tax liability generates a $150,000 research credit. The most valuable election is:

choices.A: Carry the credit forward 20 years under §39
choices.B: Elect under §41(h) to apply up to $500,000 against employer payroll tax ($250,000 against Social Security, the rest against Medicare)
choices.C: Elect §280C to reduce the credit by 21%
choices.D: Carry the credit back one year

questions.why: A qualified small business (under $5M gross receipts and no gross receipts more than five years back) can convert the credit into payroll tax cash via Form 8974. The election must be made on a timely filed original return; it cannot be made on an amended return.
